commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Add group_matmul and group_mmt4d ops (#24909)

# What & why

This PR introduces a new `group_matmul` operation, to be the IREE
equivalent of Torch's
[grouped_mm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.functional.grouped_mm.html).
It's purpose is to enable efficient inference of Mixture-of-Experts
models. The op is superficially similar to `linalg.matmul` and
`linalg.batch_matmul`, but cannot be expressed as a pure
`linalg.generic` without masking inactive elements, so I believe it
belongs here in LinalgExt. The description in LinalgExtOps.td gives more
info.

# How

1) We add the standard matmul encodings to LHS, RHS and result of our op
in SetEncoding.cpp
2) We define an auxillary `group_mmt4d` op - the grouped equivalent of
`mmt4d`
3) In MaterializeEncodingPatterns.cpp, we convert `group_matmul` to
`group_mmt4d`
4) We implement the tiling interface for `group_mmt4d`
5) After workgroup tiling, we add a `DecomposeGroupMmt4DPass`, which
turns `group_mmt4d` into `mmt4d` + some extra ops
a) if all input rows of a tile belong to the same expert, we just slice
+ `mmt4d`
b) otherwise, we loop over experts; for each of them we mask out rows
that don't belong to it

# Performance

Preliminary benchmarks have shown speed close to a matmul of comparable
shape. This is expected since:
- decomposition of `group_mmt4d` happens after workgroup tiling, so the
op turns into a single dispatch
 - there is no control flow on the host side
- the number of tiles containing a boundary between experts is limited:
(5a) is much more common than (5b)
- only the weights of the active experts need are accessed - no wasted
memory bandwidth

# Known shortcomings / future work
 - only LLVMCPU backend is supported currently
   - dynamic tile sizes (RVV & SVE) not implemented
 - for compilation to succeed, you must have enabled:
   - data tiling
   - distribution tiling (on by default)
 - LHS and RHS must be floats
- integer operands could result in an identity layout (not implemented)
- the attribute placed on `group_mmt4d` to support the narrow-N
transpose is an ugly hack
- this will no longer be needed once we can lower to `inner_tiled`
instead
- both ops implemented here could possibly be unified into some kind of
`group_contract`
- by analogy to
[linalg.contract](https://mlir.llvm.org/docs/Dialects/Linalg/#linalgcontract-linalgcontractop)
- instead of passing in expert offsets, perhaps LHS should just be a
proper [ragged
tensor](https://iree.dev/reference/mlir-dialects/TensorExt/#iree_tensor_extcast_to_ragged_shape-tensorextcasttoraggedshapeop)?
   - this feature is still work-in-progress IIUC
 - gather/scatter should be fused with this op

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Add group_matmul and group_mmt4d ops (#24909)

# What & why

This PR introduces a new `group_matmul` operation, to be the IREE
equivalent of Torch's
[grouped_mm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.functional.grouped_mm.html).
It's purpose is to enable efficient inference of Mixture-of-Experts
models. The op is superficially similar to `linalg.matmul` and
`linalg.batch_matmul`, but cannot be expressed as a pure
`linalg.generic` without masking inactive elements, so I believe it
belongs here in LinalgExt. The description in LinalgExtOps.td gives more
info.

# How

1) We add the standard matmul encodings to LHS, RHS and result of our op
in SetEncoding.cpp
2) We define an auxillary `group_mmt4d` op - the grouped equivalent of
`mmt4d`
3) In MaterializeEncodingPatterns.cpp, we convert `group_matmul` to
`group_mmt4d`
4) We implement the tiling interface for `group_mmt4d`
5) After workgroup tiling, we add a `DecomposeGroupMmt4DPass`, which
turns `group_mmt4d` into `mmt4d` + some extra ops
a) if all input rows of a tile belong to the same expert, we just slice
+ `mmt4d`
b) otherwise, we loop over experts; for each of them we mask out rows
that don't belong to it

# Performance

Preliminary benchmarks have shown speed close to a matmul of comparable
shape. This is expected since:
- decomposition of `group_mmt4d` happens after workgroup tiling, so the
op turns into a single dispatch
 - there is no control flow on the host side
- the number of tiles containing a boundary between experts is limited:
(5a) is much more common than (5b)
- only the weights of the active experts need are accessed - no wasted
memory bandwidth

# Known shortcomings / future work
 - only LLVMCPU backend is supported currently
   - dynamic tile sizes (RVV & SVE) not implemented
 - for compilation to succeed, you must have enabled:
   - data tiling
   - distribution tiling (on by default)
 - LHS and RHS must be floats
- integer operands could result in an identity layout (not implemented)
- the attribute placed on `group_mmt4d` to support the narrow-N
transpose is an ugly hack
- this will no longer be needed once we can lower to `inner_tiled`
instead
- both ops implemented here could possibly be unified into some kind of
`group_contract`
- by analogy to
[linalg.contract](https://mlir.llvm.org/docs/Dialects/Linalg/#linalgcontract-linalgcontractop)
- instead of passing in expert offsets, perhaps LHS should just be a
proper [ragged
tensor](https://iree.dev/reference/mlir-dialects/TensorExt/#iree_tensor_extcast_to_ragged_shape-tensorextcasttoraggedshapeop)?
   - this feature is still work-in-progress IIUC
 - gather/scatter should be fused with this op

4) We implement the tiling interface for `group_mmt4d`
5) After workgroup tiling, we add a `DecomposeGroupMmt4DPass`, which
turns `group_mmt4d` into `mmt4d` + some extra ops
a) if all input rows of a tile belong to the same expert, we just slice
+ `mmt4d`
b) otherwise, we loop over experts; for each of them we mask out rows
that don't belong to it

# Performance

Preliminary benchmarks have shown speed close to a matmul of comparable
shape. This is expected since:
- decomposition of `group_mmt4d` happens after workgroup tiling, so the
op turns into a single dispatch
 - there is no control flow on the host side
- the number of tiles containing a boundary between experts is limited:
(5a) is much more common than (5b)
- only the weights of the active experts need are accessed - no wasted
memory bandwidth

 - only LLVMCPU backend is supported currently
   - dynamic tile sizes (RVV & SVE) not implemented

   - data tiling
   - distribution tiling (on by default)

- integer operands could result in an identity layout (not implemented)
- the attribute placed on `group_mmt4d` to support the narrow-N
transpose is an ugly hack
- this will no longer be needed once we can lower to `inner_tiled`
instead
- both ops implemented here could possibly be unified into some kind of
`group_contract`
- by analogy to
[linalg.contract](https://mlir.llvm.org/docs/Dialects/Linalg/#linalgcontract-linalgcontractop)
- instead of passing in expert offsets, perhaps LHS should just be a
proper [ragged
tensor](https://iree.dev/reference/mlir-dialects/TensorExt/#iree_tensor_extcast_to_ragged_shape-tensorextcasttoraggedshapeop)?
   - this feature is still work-in-progress IIUC
 - gather/scatter should be fused with this op

commit_message:
[Runtime] Fix shift-count-overflow in next_power_of_two on 32-bit targets

On 32-bit targets, iree_host_size_t and iree_device_size_t are only
32 bits wide. The `value |= value >> 32;` statement in
iree_host_size_next_power_of_two() and
iree_device_size_next_power_of_two() then fails to compile with
-Werror=shift-count-overflow. This happens even though the code is
inside an `if (sizeof(...) == 8)` branch that never runs on those
targets: the compiler still checks it.

This change splits the 32-bit shift into two 16-bit shifts,
`(value >> 16) >> 16`. The result is the same on 64-bit targets, and
no shift is ever as wide as the type on 32-bit targets, so the
warning goes away.

Fixes #25134

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Moritz Riesterer <moritz.riesterer@nxp.com>
name: pre-commit

On 32-bit targets, iree_host_size_t and iree_device_size_t are only
32 bits wide. The `value |= value >> 32;` statement in
iree_host_size_next_power_of_two() and
iree_device_size_next_power_of_two() then fails to compile with
-Werror=shift-count-overflow. This happens even though the code is
inside an `if (sizeof(...) == 8)` branch that never runs on those
targets: the compiler still checks it.

This change splits the 32-bit shift into two 16-bit shifts,
`(value >> 16) >> 16`. The result is the same on 64-bit targets, and
no shift is ever as wide as the type on 32-bit targets, so the
warning goes away.

Fixes #25134

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Moritz Riesterer <moritz.riesterer@nxp.com>
name: linux_x64_clang / linux_x64_clang

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Add group_matmul and group_mmt4d ops (#24909)

# What & why

This PR introduces a new `group_matmul` operation, to be the IREE
equivalent of Torch's
[grouped_mm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.functional.grouped_mm.html).
It's purpose is to enable efficient inference of Mixture-of-Experts
models. The op is superficially similar to `linalg.matmul` and
`linalg.batch_matmul`, but cannot be expressed as a pure
`linalg.generic` without masking inactive elements, so I believe it
belongs here in LinalgExt. The description in LinalgExtOps.td gives more
info.

# How

1) We add the standard matmul encodings to LHS, RHS and result of our op
in SetEncoding.cpp
2) We define an auxillary `group_mmt4d` op - the grouped equivalent of
`mmt4d`
3) In MaterializeEncodingPatterns.cpp, we convert `group_matmul` to
`group_mmt4d`
4) We implement the tiling interface for `group_mmt4d`
5) After workgroup tiling, we add a `DecomposeGroupMmt4DPass`, which
turns `group_mmt4d` into `mmt4d` + some extra ops
a) if all input rows of a tile belong to the same expert, we just slice
+ `mmt4d`
b) otherwise, we loop over experts; for each of them we mask out rows
that don't belong to it

# Performance

Preliminary benchmarks have shown speed close to a matmul of comparable
shape. This is expected since:
- decomposition of `group_mmt4d` happens after workgroup tiling, so the
op turns into a single dispatch
 - there is no control flow on the host side
- the number of tiles containing a boundary between experts is limited:
(5a) is much more common than (5b)
- only the weights of the active experts need are accessed - no wasted
memory bandwidth

# Known shortcomings / future work
 - only LLVMCPU backend is supported currently
   - dynamic tile sizes (RVV & SVE) not implemented
 - for compilation to succeed, you must have enabled:
   - data tiling
   - distribution tiling (on by default)
 - LHS and RHS must be floats
- integer operands could result in an identity layout (not implemented)
- the attribute placed on `group_mmt4d` to support the narrow-N
transpose is an ugly hack
- this will no longer be needed once we can lower to `inner_tiled`
instead
- both ops implemented here could possibly be unified into some kind of
`group_contract`
- by analogy to
[linalg.contract](https://mlir.llvm.org/docs/Dialects/Linalg/#linalgcontract-linalgcontractop)
- instead of passing in expert offsets, perhaps LHS should just be a
proper [ragged
tensor](https://iree.dev/reference/mlir-dialects/TensorExt/#iree_tensor_extcast_to_ragged_shape-tensorextcasttoraggedshapeop)?
   - this feature is still work-in-progress IIUC
 - gather/scatter should be fused with this op

Assisted-by: Codex

Signed-off-by: Maksymilian B. Knust <knust@roofline.ai>
name: linux_x64_gcc

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Add group_matmul and group_mmt4d ops (#24909)

# What & why

This PR introduces a new `group_matmul` operation, to be the IREE
equivalent of Torch's
[grouped_mm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.functional.grouped_mm.html).
It's purpose is to enable efficient inference of Mixture-of-Experts
models. The op is superficially similar to `linalg.matmul` and
`linalg.batch_matmul`, but cannot be expressed as a pure
`linalg.generic` without masking inactive elements, so I believe it
belongs here in LinalgExt. The description in LinalgExtOps.td gives more
info.

# How

1) We add the standard matmul encodings to LHS, RHS and result of our op
in SetEncoding.cpp
2) We define an auxillary `group_mmt4d` op - the grouped equivalent of
`mmt4d`
3) In MaterializeEncodingPatterns.cpp, we convert `group_matmul` to
`group_mmt4d`
4) We implement the tiling interface for `group_mmt4d`
5) After workgroup tiling, we add a `DecomposeGroupMmt4DPass`, which
turns `group_mmt4d` into `mmt4d` + some extra ops
a) if all input rows of a tile belong to the same expert, we just slice
+ `mmt4d`
b) otherwise, we loop over experts; for each of them we mask out rows
that don't belong to it

# Performance

Preliminary benchmarks have shown speed close to a matmul of comparable
shape. This is expected since:
- decomposition of `group_mmt4d` happens after workgroup tiling, so the
op turns into a single dispatch
 - there is no control flow on the host side
- the number of tiles containing a boundary between experts is limited:
(5a) is much more common than (5b)
- only the weights of the active experts need are accessed - no wasted
memory bandwidth

# Known shortcomings / future work
 - only LLVMCPU backend is supported currently
   - dynamic tile sizes (RVV & SVE) not implemented
 - for compilation to succeed, you must have enabled:
   - data tiling
   - distribution tiling (on by default)
 - LHS and RHS must be floats
- integer operands could result in an identity layout (not implemented)
- the attribute placed on `group_mmt4d` to support the narrow-N
transpose is an ugly hack
- this will no longer be needed once we can lower to `inner_tiled`
instead
- both ops implemented here could possibly be unified into some kind of
`group_contract`
- by analogy to
[linalg.contract](https://mlir.llvm.org/docs/Dialects/Linalg/#linalgcontract-linalgcontractop)
- instead of passing in expert offsets, perhaps LHS should just be a
proper [ragged
tensor](https://iree.dev/reference/mlir-dialects/TensorExt/#iree_tensor_extcast_to_ragged_shape-tensorextcasttoraggedshapeop)?
   - this feature is still work-in-progress IIUC
 - gather/scatter should be fused with this op

commit_message:
[Torch] Expose non-finite initializer option (#25138)

I ran into this while compiling a PyTorch training graph through
`Turbine → IREE → WebGPU` inside JupyterLite. In a LLVM/MLIR 23.1.2
wasm64 build, a minimal FP32 l`og_softmax` on a 4×10 tensor aborts in
Tint with `TINT_ASSERT(std::isfinite(v.value))`. Selecting Torch-MLIR’s
existing finite-initializer option allows it to compile successfully.

Torch-MLIR already provides `allow-non-finites=false` for using finite
initializers. This exposes the option as
`--iree-torch-allow-non-finites` and forwards it through the existing
Torch-to-Linalg, Torch-to-TMTensor and ONNX conversions. We should keep
the default as true.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

[Torch] Expose non-finite initializer option (#25138)

I ran into this while compiling a PyTorch training graph through
`Turbine → IREE → WebGPU` inside JupyterLite. In a LLVM/MLIR 23.1.2
wasm64 build, a minimal FP32 l`og_softmax` on a 4×10 tensor aborts in
Tint with `TINT_ASSERT(std::isfinite(v.value))`. Selecting Torch-MLIR’s
existing finite-initializer option allows it to compile successfully.

Torch-MLIR already provides `allow-non-finites=false` for using finite
initializers. This exposes the option as
`--iree-torch-allow-non-finites` and forwards it through the existing
Torch-to-Linalg, Torch-to-TMTensor and ONNX conversions. We should keep
the default as true.

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Add group_matmul and group_mmt4d ops (#24909)

# What & why

This PR introduces a new `group_matmul` operation, to be the IREE
equivalent of Torch's
[grouped_mm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.functional.grouped_mm.html).
It's purpose is to enable efficient inference of Mixture-of-Experts
models. The op is superficially similar to `linalg.matmul` and
`linalg.batch_matmul`, but cannot be expressed as a pure
`linalg.generic` without masking inactive elements, so I believe it
belongs here in LinalgExt. The description in LinalgExtOps.td gives more
info.

# How

1) We add the standard matmul encodings to LHS, RHS and result of our op
in SetEncoding.cpp
2) We define an auxillary `group_mmt4d` op - the grouped equivalent of
`mmt4d`
3) In MaterializeEncodingPatterns.cpp, we convert `group_matmul` to
`group_mmt4d`
4) We implement the tiling interface for `group_mmt4d`
5) After workgroup tiling, we add a `DecomposeGroupMmt4DPass`, which
turns `group_mmt4d` into `mmt4d` + some extra ops
a) if all input rows of a tile belong to the same expert, we just slice
+ `mmt4d`
b) otherwise, we loop over experts; for each of them we mask out rows
that don't belong to it

# Performance

Preliminary benchmarks have shown speed close to a matmul of comparable
shape. This is expected since:
- decomposition of `group_mmt4d` happens after workgroup tiling, so the
op turns into a single dispatch
 - there is no control flow on the host side
- the number of tiles containing a boundary between experts is limited:
(5a) is much more common than (5b)
- only the weights of the active experts need are accessed - no wasted
memory bandwidth

# Known shortcomings / future work
 - only LLVMCPU backend is supported currently
   - dynamic tile sizes (RVV & SVE) not implemented
 - for compilation to succeed, you must have enabled:
   - data tiling
   - distribution tiling (on by default)
 - LHS and RHS must be floats
- integer operands could result in an identity layout (not implemented)
- the attribute placed on `group_mmt4d` to support the narrow-N
transpose is an ugly hack
- this will no longer be needed once we can lower to `inner_tiled`
instead
- both ops implemented here could possibly be unified into some kind of
`group_contract`
- by analogy to
[linalg.contract](https://mlir.llvm.org/docs/Dialects/Linalg/#linalgcontract-linalgcontractop)
- instead of passing in expert offsets, perhaps LHS should just be a
proper [ragged
tensor](https://iree.dev/reference/mlir-dialects/TensorExt/#iree_tensor_extcast_to_ragged_shape-tensorextcasttoraggedshapeop)?
   - this feature is still work-in-progress IIUC
 - gather/scatter should be fused with this op

Assisted-by: Codex
